STAGE: scope + evidence audit of all four proposals (rank-2026-10-v1).
READ: frozen bundle items E4-E13 shared by all four, plus each proposal's own E1-E3/E12-E13 and specification.
OBSERVED (shared, load-bearing): (i) E6 width-20 beam survival: best prefix-level diagnostics sit at 0.062-0.064 (l1_br_euclid 0.06207, l1_only 0.06233, resample 0.06363) i.e. right at the 0.065 gate, while behaviour-direction latent moves are worse: successor_geodesic_coarse 0.05500, successor_geodesic_coarse_v2 0.05463, tangent_successor_residual 0.05500. (ii) E6 gold-prefix survival collapses at depth 2-3 (0.829->0.161 for euclid family; 1.000/1.000/1.000/0.068 for l1_br) so the binding loss is deep-prefix, not level-1. (iii) E8: behaviour co-clustering at small K is 0.3106 (K=16) / 0.2164 (K=32) against negative 0.1352/0.0715, i.e. small-fanout behaviour partitions keep behavioural neighbours together 2-3x more often. (iv) E5: successor concentration is strongly heterogeneous (top-1 mass 0.4375 low-entropy quintile vs 0.0543 high), so a concentration/drift signal is non-degenerate. (v) E7 teacher-forced NLL confirms T1 is free and T2/T3 carry the error.
REASONING: All four satisfy the letter of the scope contract (behaviour signal + explicit curved op + one connected pathway + named switches + testable effect). The differentiator is which one attacks the failure the evidence actually locates (depth-2/3 prefix structure) rather than re-moving level-1 latents into the family the evidence already shows at 0.055.
OPEN: per-proposal placement and reasons.

STAGE: per-proposal placement.
READ: each proposal's spec + risks against E5/E6/E7/E8.
OBSERVED/REASONING:
- behtree-geocut-sid: only proposal that changes which items may share a token AND allocates fanout by a behaviour significance test (2-sigma null cut). Directly matches E8 (small-K behaviour co-clustering 0.2164 vs 0.0715) and E6 (depth-2/3 survival collapse). Genuine curved quantization (exact Poincare distance to gyrobarycentric anchors, logits = -d_P, geodesic-hyperplane/Klein-bisector splits). Risks: near-unique leaves, prefix-local token ambiguity; acknowledged. Best evidence fit. => position 1.
- holonomy-frame-sid: preserves the working L1 (E6 shows L1 already 251/256 and saturated) and only rotates deep frames; geometry is a real curved quantity (Gauss-Bonnet area -> holonomy) and behaviour sets the drift direction, which E5 says is heterogeneous. But two structural weaknesses: flat limit forces theta=0, so the geometry-off arm collapses onto the behaviour-off arm (no distinct Euclidean counterfactual), and a rigid per-prefix codebook rotation is at risk of being a relabeling (its own risk (a)/(b)). Evidence locates the problem correctly but the lever is weaker than a partition change. => position 2.
- CONCMID-GEO-SID: cheapest and has a clean distinct Euclidean arm (flat blend with same w and eta), but it only moves the level-1 quantizer input toward a successor barycentre. That is the same family the bundle already scores at 0.055 (successor_geodesic_coarse / _v2 / tangent_successor_residual) versus 0.062-0.064 for prefix-level arms; and E6 shows L1 is already fully used, so moving points there does not address the depth-2/3 collapse. Its own risk list concedes eta may be tiny and curvature may be a near-gauge. => position 3.
- HSPT-RQ: per-item Lorentz parallel transport of child codebooks with rho=||u|| gives cosh(rho) up to ~74, i.e. the transported codebook is dominated by the item's behaviour direction; the effective codebook becomes item-specific and assignment near-arbitrary. It is the transport variant of tangent_successor_residual which the bundle measures at 0.05500, and it costs 0.20-0.25 s/epoch (780-1050 s vs 571 s). Highest risk, least evidence support, same failing family. => position 4.
OPEN: nothing; final block next.

STAGE: FINAL ANSWER (complete answer block, stands alone).

RANK: behtree-geocut-sid | position=1 | reason=E8 is the decisive item: small-fanout behaviour clusters co-locate behavioural neighbours 0.2164 (K=32) and 0.3106 (K=16) against 0.0715/0.1352 for fixed negatives, and E6 shows the loss is depth-2/3 prefix survival (0.829->0.161) not level-1 (already 251/256) - this is the only proposal that reallocates fanout and token-sharing by a behaviour significance test with exact Poincare-distance assignment to gyrobarycentric anchors, so it attacks the failure the evidence locates.
RANK: holonomy-frame-sid | position=2 | reason=E6/E7 confirm the L2/L3 triple collapse (1769/2201 prefixes for 24556 items) and E5 confirms successor drift is strongly heterogeneous (top-1 mass 0.4375 vs 0.0543), so a per-prefix area-driven frame is non-degenerate; it correctly leaves the already-saturated L1 untouched, but its flat limit forces theta=0 so the geometry-off arm coincides with the behaviour-off arm, and its own risk (a)/(b) admits the rotation can reduce to a relabeling.
RANK: CONCMID-GEO-SID | position=3 | reason=It only moves the level-1 quantizer input toward a successor barycentre, which is the family E6 already scores at 0.05500 (successor_geodesic_coarse/_v2, tangent_successor_residual) versus 0.06207-0.06363 for prefix-level arms, and E6 shows L1 is already fully used (251/256) with the failure at depth 2-3, so its lever misses the binding constraint; it does have the cleanest distinct Euclidean switch (flat blend, same w and eta) and near-zero cost.
RANK: HSPT-RQ | position=4 | reason=Rho=||u|| gives cosh(rho) up to ~74 so the per-item transported codebook becomes dominated by the behaviour direction and assignment near-arbitrary (its own risk 1/2), it is the parallel-transport variant of tangent_successor_residual measured at 0.05500 in E6, and its cost (0.20-0.25 s/epoch, 780-1050 s vs 571 s) is the highest of the four with the least evidence support.
